_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Harvest is near, and cut wheat can’t sit wet, so this week’s question is a practical one: how much warning can you get of rain? Often a day, if you look up high.

replies.back: Sometimes more. The ice clouds out in front tell you what’s coming long before it gets here.

turns.them: The high floor, all ice, the grey sheets that come down after it, and a ring around the sun. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Read me the high sky.
Now you can give a farmer a timetable instead of a shrug. Next lesson, thunderstorms.
